key_insight: Creative AI should not treat expert disagreement as pure error. The paper argues that evaluator judgments in creative tasks contain two meaningful signals: shared agreement about best practices and real differences in taste.
problem_solved: Standard AI evaluation methods collapse all evaluator disagreement into noise, which breaks down in creative domains where disagreement is often legitimate. This paper addresses how to evaluate creative AI while preserving both consensus and subjective diversity.
method: Introduces the Human Creativity Benchmark (HCB) to separate evaluator feedback into convergence and divergence.
Measures where professionals align on quality signals versus where personal taste leads to valid disagreement.
Reframes disagreement as structured information rather than evaluation failure.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, HCB offers a more realistic way to assess creative systems such as writing, design, and ideation models. It can improve benchmark validity by matching evaluation to the nature of the task.
visual_elements: Split-flow diagram showing 'convergence' vs. 'divergence' in evaluator judgments
Side-by-side comparison of traditional evaluation vs. HCB-style evaluation
Icon set representing taste, expertise, and consensus
Simple benchmark pipeline graphic illustrating how HCB separates signals
paper_authors: Aspen Hopkins, Allison Nulty, Alexandria Minetti, Anoop Pakki, Angad Singh
